extracted.intended_audience: students and instructors of commutative algebra (advanced undergraduates / graduate level)
extracted.subtask_description: Worked solutions and statements of exercises in commutative algebra (localization, integrality, primes, dimension, Noetherian/Jacobson properties, primary decomposition) intended to demonstrate and prove standard criteria and equivalences used in the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting equality of submodules by localizations at maximal ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: M = N if M_m = N_m for every maximal ideal m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First reduce to the case M ⊇ N; use localization and earlier results (12.16,13.16) to deduce equality globally from equality at all maximal ideals; replace N by M+N for the general case using (12.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of reduced rings via localization
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are equivalent: (1) R is reduced. (2) S^{-1}R is reduced for all multiplicatively closed sets S. (3) R_m is reduced for all maximal ideals m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nil(R) behaviour under localization (11.16), trivial implications (2)⇒(3), and (13.16)/(12.2) to deduce (3)⇒(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comaximality of minimal primes when localizations are domains
rubrics_metrics.description: If R_p is a domain for every prime p, then the minimal primes of R are pairwise comaximal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two minimal primes p and q were not comaximal they would survive in some R_m, contradicting R_m being a domain with unique minimal prime ⟨0⟩.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product decomposition when localizations are domains and minimal primes finite
rubrics_metrics.description: Rp is a domain for every prime p and the set of minimal primes is finite iff R is a finite product ∏_{i=1}^n R_i where each R_i is a domain (and the R_i are R/p_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form canonical map φ: R → ∏_{p minimal} R/p; injectivity by (3.28) and surjectivity by (1) plus Chinese Remainder Theorem (1.13); converse uses localization and projection arguments (12.10, 2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generators tested locally at maximal ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements m_1,…,m_r generate module M iff their images generate M_m for every maximal ideal m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the natural map R^{ set{m_i}} → M and use (13.20) and localization facts (12.10, 4.10(1)) to reduce surjectivity to each localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of a flat algebra at a prime is faithfully flat over localized base
rubrics_metrics.description: If R → R' is a flat algebra, p' a prime of R' with contraction p in R, then R'_{p'} is faithfully flat over R_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that R'_{p} is flat over R_p (13.23) and factor R'_{p'} as R'_{p} localized at p'R'_{p}; a flat local homomorphism is faithfully flat (9.10(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free of rank n iff finitely generated and locally free at maximals
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-module P is locally free of rank n iff P is finitely generated and P_m ≅ R_m^n for every maximal ideal m. Moreover for any prime p there exists f ∉ p with P_f ≅ R_f^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use finite generation (13.27), localization arguments (12.5,12.20,10.4) and patching via elements f to produce desired local trivializations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free over semilocal ring is free
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is semilocal and P is a locally free module of rank n, then P is free of rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P is finitely presented and trivializes at each maximal ideal; semilocal condition allows global freeness (13.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of primes and maximal ideals under integral extensions with a unique prime above
rubrics_metrics.description: If R ⊂ R' is integral and p ∈ Spec(R) has exactly one prime p' of R' lying over it then: (a) p'R'_{p'} is the unique maximal ideal of R'_{p'}. (b) The nonmaximal elements of R'_{p'} are units (i.e., the maximal ideal consists of nonunits). (c) R'_{p'} is integral over R_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize the integral extension (11.23), use that Rp is local with unique maximal ideal and apply properties of integral extensions and going-up/lying-over to identify primes in the localization (14.3,11.18,11.7,11.28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-integrality when there are multiple primes over a prime
rubrics_metrics.description: If R⊂R' is integral extension of domains and there are at least two distinct primes p' and q' of R' lying over p, then for y ∈ q' ackslash p' the element 1/y is not integral over R_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume 1/y integral and deduce a contradiction by clearing denominators and using the fact q'∩R = p (14.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrality of localization in branched quadratic extension depends on characteristic
rubrics_metrics.description: For R'=k[X] with R=k[Y], Y=X^2, and p=(Y-1) in R with p'=(X-1) in R': R'_{p'} is integral over R_p iff there is exactly one prime of R' over p; this happens in characteristic 2 but not in odd characteristic (since X+1 gives a second prime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit the second prime when char≠2, and use (14.5) and (14.4) to characterize integrality of localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of z:div(R) and localizations at minimal primes in reduced rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is reduced and Min(R) denotes minimal primes, then z:div(R) = ⋃_{p∈Min(R)} p, and for p∈Min(R) we have R_p = Frac(R/p) (a field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior results: Rp reduced with unique prime pRp, hence a field; relations between zero-divisors and minimal primes (14.10–14.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalences involving total quotient ring and minimal primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming Min(R) finite and K the total quotient ring, the following are equivalent: (1) R is reduced. (2) z:div(R)=⋃_{p∈Min(R)} p. (3) K/pK = Frac(R/p) for each minimal p and K = ∏_{p∈Min(R)} K/pK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use localization, structure of K as localization at non-zero-divisors, and previous facts about reduced rings and fields (14.12–14.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for freeness via dimensions over residue and component fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a reduced local ring with residue field k and finitely many minimal primes. A finitely generated module P is free of rank r iff dim_k(P⊗_A k) = r and dim_{K(p)}(P⊗_A K(p)) = r for each minimal prime p (K(p)=Frac(A/p)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use generation by r elements, examine kernel M of presentation, tensor with component fields and total quotient ring to deduce M=0 (14.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Descent of freeness along surjective Spec map
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the hypotheses of the previous item, if B is an A-algebra with Spec(B) → Spec(A) surjective, then P is free of rank r over A iff P⊗_A B is free of rank r over B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use behavior of dimensions after tensoring with fraction fields of residue fields and surjectivity of Spec map to lift rank conditions (14.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of normal rings
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring R with total quotient ring K and finite minimal primes, equivalent conditions: (1) R is normal. (2) R is reduced and integrally closed in K. (3) R is a finite product of normal domains R_i (and R_i ≅ R/p_j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integrality and normalization arguments, decomposing K into product over minimal primes and applying integrally closed conditions (14.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-integrality example for finite-field quotient algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Given k = F_q and R = k[X,Y]/⟨X^qY - XY^q⟩ with residues x,y and P = k[y], the ring R is not module-finite over P (so x is not integral over P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No polynomial multiple of f is monic in X, so x cannot be integral over P (10.18); reduction for general a∈k uses change of variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrality conditions for chosen generators in a quotient algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: In R = k[X,Y,Z]/⟨X^2 - Y^3 -1, XZ-1⟩ with t = x + a y + b z and P = k[t], x and y are always integral over P for any a,b; z is integral over P iff b ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive explicit integral equations: xz=1 gives relations; raise to powers and use tower property. For z, express z if b≠0; for b=0 get contradiction with integrally closed polynomial ring (15.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert Nullstellensatz (algebraic form)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f vanishes at every zero in K^n of f_1,…,f_r (K algebraically closed), then there exist g_1,…,g_r and integer N≥1 with f^N = g_1 f_1 + … + g_r f_r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue by considering the ideal a=⟨f_1,…,f_r⟩ and maximal ideals m containing a; embed residue fields into K and apply weak Nullstellensatz to show f∈m for every such m, then use Hilbert's Nullstellensatz (15.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension drops on nonzero prime quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a domain of finite dimension r and p is a nonzero prime, then dim(R/p) < r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A chain of primes in R/p lifts to a chain in R strictly shorter than maximal chain length (15.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariance of Krull dimension under integral extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If R′ is integral over R, then dim(R) = dim(R′).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use going-up and going-down / incomparability (14.3) to lift/contract chains of primes in both directions (15.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension preserved under inverting a nonzero element in a finitely generated domain
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a finitely generated k-domain and f≠0, then dim(R) = dim(R_f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both have the same fraction field; dimension equals transcendence degree over k (15.16, 15.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull dimension bounds for polynomial ring
rubrics_metrics.description: For any ring R, 1 + dim(R) ≤ dim(R[X]) ≤ 1 + 2 dim(R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct chains via extension of chains in R; analyze fibers over primes and use that k(p)[X] is a PID with dimension 1 to bound lengths (15.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions/characterizations of very dense subsets and Jacobson spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: A subset X_0 of a topological space X is very dense iff it meets every nonempty locally closed subset; equivalent to: (2) every closed set F satisfies F = closure(F∩X_0); (3) the map U↦U∩X_0 from opens of X to opens of X_0 is bijective. X is Jacobson iff closed points are very dense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove equivalences by manipulations of open/closed sets and complements (15.22). For rings, translate to Jacobson ring condition (15.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullstellensatz-style statement over Z and finite fields
rubrics_metrics.description: If a polynomial f∈Z[X_1,…,X_n] vanishes at every zero in K^n of f_1,…,f_r for every finite field K, then there exist g_i and N≥1 with f^N = ∑ g_i f_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to showing f∈m for some maximal ideal m containing the ideal; residue fields of maximal ideals of Z[X] are finite (15.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral extensions preserve Jacobson property
rubrics_metrics.description: If R′ is integral over R and R is Jacobson, then R′ is Jacobson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ideal a′⊂R′ and f∉a′, pass to R[f] and its maximal ideal avoiding f, then lift prime maximal ideals via integrality and going-up (15.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobson property under localization and filtered colimits—counterexamples
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) R_f is Jacobson if R is. (2) S^{-1}R need not be Jacobson in general (counterexample: Z localized at p). (3) Filtered direct limits of Jacobson rings need not be Jacobson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples Z (Jacobson) but Z⟨p⟩ not Jacobson and filtered limit producing Z⟨p⟩ to show failures (15.27).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local criterion for locally free modules over reduced Jacobson rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is reduced Jacobson with finitely many minimal primes and P finitely generated, then P is locally free of rank r iff for every maximal ideal m we have dim_{R/m}(P/mP)=r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to checking over localizations at maximal ideals and use structure of minimal primes and component fields; uses (13.28) and (14.14) (15.28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation of finitely generated ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a is finitely generated, then every set of generators of a contains a finite subset that generates a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express the original finite generating set in terms of the given generating set to select finitely many elements (16.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian property descends from polynomial ring
rubrics_metrics.description: If R[X] is Noetherian, then R is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R ≅ R[X]/⟨X⟩ and quotient of Noetherian ring is Noetherian (16.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterexample to equality of submodules from equal images under quotient and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If L→M→N exact and two submodules M1,M2 satisfy (L)(M1)=(L)(M2) and (M1+L)/(L)=(M2+L)/(L), it need not follow M1=M2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit counterexample using R⊕R with specially chosen lines (16.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherianity under products of quotient conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: If ideals a_1,…,a_r of R satisfy that each R/a_i is Noetherian and intersection ∩ a_i = 0 then R is Noetherian; more generally if direct sum conditions hold and kernels identified, deduce R Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that R injects into ⊕ R/a_i and that each quotient is Noetherian as R-module (16.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether's theorem on invariant rings under finite group action
rubrics_metrics.description: If a finite group G acts on a domain R and R is algebra-finite over a field k, then the invariant subring R^G is algebra-finite over k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that R is integral over the subring generated by invariants and finiteness of module extension (10.17, 16.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite-dimensional k-algebras are Noetherian and Artinian
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a k-algebra finite dimensional as a k-vector space, then R is Noetherian and Artinian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideals are subspaces; chains stabilize by finite dimensionality (16.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example module Artinian but not Noetherian
rubrics_metrics.description: For prime p, M = Z[1/p]/Z has the property every Z-submodule is either finite or whole M, hence M is Artinian but not Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show possible submodules characterized by largest exponent and descending chains stabilize while generation fails (16.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artinian domain is a field; primes in Artinian ring are maximal
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Artinian and a domain then R is a field; in any Artinian ring every prime ideal is maximal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stabilization of powers of an element to find inverse; quotienting by prime yields Artinian domain hence field (16.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes of finite direct sum
rubrics_metrics.description: Ass(M_1 ⊕ … ⊕ M_r) = Ass(M_1) ∪ … ∪ Ass(M_r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed by induction using exact sequences and (17.5) (17.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of submodules whose Ass unions are proper subset of Ass(M)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist modules M and submodules L,N with L+N=M but Ass(L)∪Ass(N) ⫋ Ass(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete example: R=Z, M=Z/2 ⊕ Z with chosen submodules L,N (17.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes are minimal when all localizations are domains
rubrics_metrics.description: If R_p is a domain for every prime p then every associated prime of R is minimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize an associated prime and use that Ass(R_p) = {0} when Rp domain, then deduce minimality (17.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication by x preserves intersection with submodule when x avoids Ass(M/N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R Noetherian, M module, N submodule. If x ∉ p for every p ∈ Ass(M/N) then xM ∩ N = xN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction via residue class and the fact x avoids zero-divisors on M/N (17.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primes minimal over an ideal are associated and finite in number
rubrics_metrics.description: For Noetherian R and ideal a, the primes minimal containing a are associated to a and there are finitely many of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that a = Ann(R/a) and properties linking Supp and Ass (17.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable chains and associated primes in cyclic Z-modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of acceptable chains for modules of the form Z and Z/12Z; acceptable chain corresponds to prime ideals and yields Ass(M) equal to primes appearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work out concrete possibilities for divisors and prime factors (17.22–17.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of a principal prime generated by nonzerodivisor are primary; conversely in Noetherian rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If p=⟨p⟩ is principal generated by a nonzerodivisor then p^n is p-primary for all n>0. Conversely in a Noetherian ring every p-primary ideal q equals p^n for some n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact sequences and analyze Ass of quotient; conversely use minimal n with p^n⊂q and argue by maximality of exponent (18.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of non-primary ideals satisfying weak squared-factor property
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: a=⟨X^2, XY⟩ in k[X,Y] is not primary (since X∉a, Y∉a but XY∈a), yet satisfies: if ab∈a then a^2∈a or b^2∈a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize a has radical ⟨X⟩ and check the squared-factor condition by divisibility by X (18.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse images of primary ideals under ring homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ:R→R' is a homomorphism of Noetherian rings and q⊂R' is p'-primary then φ^{-1}(q) is φ^{-1}(p')-primary in R. Converse holds if φ is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify primary property by lifting relations and using integrality of inverse/image operations and radicals (18.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing primary decompositions and irredundance via examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples (e.g., a=⟨XY, X-YZ⟩ in k[X,Y,Z]) showing explicit irredundant primary decompositions and verifying primality/primary nature of components (q1=⟨X,Z⟩, q2=⟨Y^2, X-YZ⟩).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check containment both ways and use homomorphisms to simpler rings to identify primary components via preimage of principal primary ideals (18.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary decomposition of zero in product of domains
rubrics_metrics.description: If R = R' × R'' is product of two domains, then ⟨0⟩ = p' ∩ p'' where p' = 0×R'' and p'' = R'×0, and this is an irredundant primary decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each component is prime and necessary (18.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submodule of elements killed by powers of an ideal and support characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: For Noetherian R, M finitely generated and ideal a, define a(M) = { m∈M | a^n m = 0 for some n≥1 }. Then (1) a(M) equals intersection of primary components Q_i whose primes contain a in any primary decomposition of 0 in M. (2) Equivalently, a(M) is set of m whose image in M_p is zero for every prime p with a ⊄ p (i.e., support lies in V(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use primary decomposition of 0 in M, Nakayama-type localization arguments, and relate vanishing in localizations to containment in primary components (18.21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovering submodule from its localizations at associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: If R Noetherian, M finitely generated, and N⊂M, then N = ⋂_{p∈Ass(M/N)} (preimage in M of N_p) (equivalently intersection of p-primary components corresponding to Ass(M/N)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an irredundant primary decomposition N=⋂ Q_i with Ass(M/N)={p_i} and localize to identify components (18.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of symbolic powers
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) The nth symbolic power p^{(n)} = (p^n)S where S=R ackslash p is the p-primary component of p^n. (2) p^{(m+n)} is the p-primary component of p^{(m)} p^{(n)}. (3) p^{(n)} = p^n iff p^n is p-primary. (4) For any p-primary q, q ⊂ p^{(n)} for all large n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prime avoidance and saturation/localization arguments to identify p-primary components and multiplicative behaviour (18.26).
